L12: A353847
L13: 
L14: Composition run-sum transformation in terms of standard composition numbers. The a(k)-th composition in standard order is the sequence of run-sums of the k-th composition in standard order. Takes each index of a row of cite4†A066099 to the index of the row consisting of its run-sums.

L25: COMMENTS
L26: Every sequence can be uniquely split into a sequence of non-overlapping runs. For example, the runs of (2,2,1,1,1,3,2,2) are ((2,2),(1,1,1),(3),(2,2)), with sums (4,3,3,4).
L27: 
L28: The k-th composition in standard order (graded reverse-lexicographic, cite4†A066099 ) is obtained by taking the set of positions of 1's in the reversed binary expansion of k, prepending 0, taking first differences, and reversing again. This gives a bijective correspondence between nonnegative integers and integer compositions.

L84: MATHEMATICA
L85: 
L86: stc[n_]:=Differences[Prepend[Join@@ Position[Reverse[IntegerDigits[n, 2]], 1], 0]]//Reverse;
L87: 
L88: stcinv[q_]:=Total[2^(Accumulate[Reverse[q]])]/2;
L89: 
L90: Table[stcinv[Total/@Split[stc[n]]], {n, 0, 100}]
